summary: chai-leaf ships obfuscated import-time payload referencing AWS/SSH credential paths under a pino cosplay
details: chai-leaf@1.4.6 presents itself as a JSON logger (ships pino's README, docs/, and index.d.ts; declares an unrelated 'vulnerability management' description; author metadata points to jsonspack.com), but its main entry index.js unconditionally requires lib/config.js, a 3.5MB single-line obfuscator.io bundle (hex-mangled identifiers, rotating string array of ~20708 entries, embedded base64 decoder). The obfuscated bundle contains literal '.aws' and '.ssh' string references — the canonical installer credential directories — together with child_process execSync and spawn call sites whose arguments are reconstructed at runtime from the string array and therefore not statically inspectable. Requiring the package causes this opaque bundle to run in the consumer's Node.js process at import time. A logger has no legitimate need for a multi-megabyte obfuscated payload, access to ~/.aws or ~/.ssh, or arbitrary shell execution; the cosplay of pino's documentation lures installers into loading a credential-harvester/dropper core.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
